page: Amazon Web Services m9g.2xlarge is an ARM-based general purpose instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and powered by AWS Graviton generation 9 processors. The instance features the ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 architecture operating at a sustained clock speed of 3.3 GHz. It is provisioned with 8 dedicated physical cores executing one thread per core, backed by 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 32.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 core-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU.

Hardware acceleration components and integrated local storage are omitted in this configuration; the instance provides no GPUs and designates local disk capacity as None, necessitating the use of remote Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes for persistent filesystem operations. Baseline network throughput is rated at 4 Gbps. Cryptographic capabilities include hardware AES acceleration, though x86-specific vector instruction sets such as AVX and AMX are naturally absent on this arm64 processor.

Benchmark measurements reveal strong single-thread efficiency and memory responsiveness. In synthetic tests, the instance records top-tier results in Geekbench single-core execution (2379.0 points), Geekbench text processing (3166.0 points), single-threaded gzip compression (36.45 GB/sec), and PassMark memory operations (4064.84 points). Conversely, multi-threaded metrics remain within median distributions, including multi-core Geekbench (12869.0 points) and stress-ng multi-core CPU capacity (16045.33 points). PassMark encryption throughput sits in the lower quartile at 2363.25 points.

Workload evaluation indicates the m9g.2xlarge functions effectively for web serving, microservices architectures, Clang software builds, and cache layers such as Redis, where it achieved 23.58 million SET operations per second. However, heavy matrix operations and large language model prompt evaluation on 7B models demonstrate lower relative throughput, making it unsuitable for GPU-dependent machine learning or storage-intensive I/O requiring raw local NVMe throughput.
description: Amazon Web Services m9g.2xlarge is an arm64 general purpose instance powered by dedicated AWS Graviton Neoverse-V3 processors running at 3.3 GHz. The instance delivers 8 vCPUs across 8 single-threaded physical cores, 32.0 GB of system memory (4.0 GB per core), and a baseline network throughput of 4 Gbps under the Nitro hypervisor. It contains no onboard GPUs and includes zero local storage, requiring network-attached EBS volumes for non-volatile storage. Benchmarks highlight upper-bracket performance in memory operations, single-core computational tasks, text processing, and decompression, while overall multi-core and static web serving tests sit within average mid-tier distributions. Due to modest multi-threaded vector expansion and the absence of direct local disk, the instance delivers high efficiency for general application backends, Redis caching, CI/CD compilation, and web applications rather than intensive matrix acceleration or localized database clusters.
